verdict.rationale: The public pricing page shows a credit-based model: credits from $5 with no subscription or expiry, plus a one-time $15 signup credit with no card required. That gives some up-front cost transparency. However, the evidence shows no actual per-task or per-browser-hour rates and no documented rate or concurrency limits. Missing for 10: explicit per-task/per-browser-hour unit prices, documented rate limits, documented concurrency limits, independent corroboration of pricing clarity.
